institutionName: Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went traveling in my gap year and when I came to Rio the world was shut down by covid. Since then I just felt like I had to go back and exchange was the perfect opportunity!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy:)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international office at puc bombed us with information about everything from the university to the weather in rio. They arfe super helpful and kind!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It wasn't too easy getting answers per mail from puc in the months leading up to the exchange. But seriously don't hesitate to drop by their office on campus if you're still confused when you get there.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing for the first 1,5 months through some far out contacts, but later I found a very nice room with some locals in Gávea close to puc. I found the apartment through Webquarto. In the puc whatsapp group Brother Carioca there is also a lot of people reaching out to find tenants!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Prioriotize living close to the metro, it will make your life so much easier and you can safe money by not ubering a lot. Gávea is chill, upper-class and close to campus, Leblon and Ipanema is rich, close to the beach and more chic and fancy, Copacabana is my personal favorite (duh) because it has everything, Leme is also very nice and chill but a bit further from campus and the metro. Flamengo/botafogo/Catete are also cool neighbourhoods, has metro stations and markets and nightlife! But pretty far from campus (closer to the centro though).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were no housing available to students, but on their site they refer to Uliving where A LOT of international students live. I have heard good stuff (rooftop pool) and bad stuff (moldy rooms) so like best of both worlds maybe?

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a real-time course selection so do yourself a favor and make a plan. The courses fills up QUICKLY so if you want or need something specifically, prioriotize adding that first and work your way down the list. Have alternatives!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I just used to course catalog to search more details about the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you avoid the late courses you have more good UV hours at the beach;)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: For me it was pretty chill. I took mostly introductory courses and courses meant for internationals, so it wasn't super complicated

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were days with just listening to the professor for 1,5 hours and days with more class discussions, and then there were suprisingly many group presentations (didn't like that).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
FIL1001: History of Philosophy
JUR1954: Internation Law and Justice (Genocide)
JUR1933: Experimental Philosophy and Jurisprudence
HIS9827: Brazilian History
SOC9173: Inequality and Diversity in Urban Contexts
LET9420: Brazilian Language and Culture: From Stereotypes to Reality
LET1280: Portuguese para Estrangeiros

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
SOC9173: Very chill course but super interesting and teaches you a lot about Rio and Brasil and the structural racism and oppression. Has field trips!
JUR1933: Super nice professor and also a very interesting subject!!
JUR1954: Loved this course, it was very heavy but I learned a lot. The professor was a guest from Canada though, so I don't know if the course will return.

Honorable mention: FIL1001 I loved the professor, she is super fun and knows everything about what she teaches but I was personally struggeling a lot with understanding what we talked about lol

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I have no clue because I did not participate in any. There is a community for internationals and locals called Brother Carioca and they do a lot of different stuff but I never went

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: BEACH!!! Bailefunk<3 visit your local friday fruitmarkets!! Weekend markets in centro! Lanchonetes! Watch football in Maracanã! Go do the trails if your're outdoorsy type. Go see live music, pagode, forró, samba. Dance<3 Learn how to play altinha on the beach!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Búzios/Cabo Frio/Arraial do Cabo north of Rio. Ilha Grande south of Rio. The Iguaçu waterfalls on the frontiers between Argentina and Brazil!!!!!!!!! The Amazon (I went to Alter do Chão, from what I have heard it's a bit more chill and vacation ish vibes, but faaaar less touristed than Manaus. Loved it.) São Paulo weekend trip, Salvador weekend trip!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In the beginning there is a lot to take in, but I quickly felt at home and find my way around it. Everything here is really laid back! Like do not stress!!! be impulsive and ready to change plans. Be late!!!! time is very relative! Brazilians also eat SOOO much and always make fun of me that I eat little (I litterally inhale my food). There is a lot of noise and music all the time which I love<333

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: the best way is the Brother Carioca group I think.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Brazilian time, and the way people will break their neck to look at you if you look very gringo. The men have NO SHAME in staring you down.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warmth, the love, the open arms, the laughs, the honesty, the sharing, the music, the food, the people<3333

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Learn the language. For real, this is the one investment in your exchange that will change your experience completely. It opens so many doors just to be able to communicate and the be curious. 
- Say yes to things even when they're out of your comfortzone, it always turns out great. 
- Think about how your actions affects society. Where do you put your money? How can you add something to the poor communities in a sustainable way? Brazil is BEAUTIFUL and fun but also violent and corrupt. As an international student you can avoid the dark sides completely, but please look into it and educate yourself and talk to the locals.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The portuguese para estrangeiros is MANDATORY and was NOT approved for credit transfer by my falculty at UCPH. This meant I had to teake 39 credits as 9 of them were worthless. Keep this in mind especially if your'e BA!
MAKE A CPF!!! will help you a lot and also if you make a PIX it will make your life so much easier!!!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting my boyfriend and falling in love<3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: feeling unsafe at night felt really restricting. It's not like it's unsafe everywhere all the time but I was not fucking around and finding out. Be aware of your surroundings at all times

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO TO BRAZIL!!!!!!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
